newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Handelsbanken Q1 profit beat expectations.
newsitem.headline: Handelsbanken Q1 profit beat expectations.

text.p: Sweden's Svenska Handelsbanken gave the first indication of the health of the fast-changing Swedish banking sector on Monday when it reported first quarter earnings that beat analysts' expectations and sent its share higher.

Operating profit after credit losses rose 14 percent to 1.73 billion crowns ($226.6 million) in the first three months of the year, beating the expected 1.64 billion a Reuter poll of 10 analysts showed.
Profit was boosted by lower loan losses as well as by higher net interest and commission income, but also by the bank's February acquisition of mortgage lender Stadshypotek for 22.9 billion crowns.
Stadshypotek was included in earnings as of February 26, the bank said, adding that it had not changed the comparison figures from the first quarter of last year to reflect the acquisition.

Handelsbanken's share jumped after the report was released and closed up 5.0 crowns at 226 crowns from its Friday close and up 2.5 crowns from 223 crowns before the figures hit stock market traders' screens.
Loan losses fell 68 percent to 130 million crowns, while net interest income rose 17 percent to 2.61 billion crowns.
"Almost half of the increase in net interest income stems from increased lending volumes, partly following the acquisition of Stadshypotek," the bank said in a statement.
"Excluding Stadshypotek, margins between deposit and lending rates were largely unchanged."
The other half of the increase, about 200 million crowns, stemmed from trading related activities, the bank said.
Net financial items declined to a six million crown gain from a 492 million crown gain. Net commission rose 18 percent to 797 million, mainly lifted by increased securities trading profits.
